description: The figure is a three-level sunburst (nested pie) chart showing the distribution of examples by abusiveness status, then by abuse type, and finally by sentiment/polarity. The innermost ring has 2 slices: “Abusive” (teal, a bit over half, roughly ~55–60%) and “Not Abusive” (pale yellow, the remainder, roughly ~40–45%). The middle ring subdivides these into 10 labeled categories total: within Abusive (teal) there are “Other” (largest, roughly ~25–30% of the whole), “Political” (next, roughly ~15–20%), “Racial” (small, ~4–6%), “Sexist” (small, ~3–5%), and “Religious” (very small, ~1–2%); within Not Abusive (yellow) there are “Other” (largest, roughly ~25–30%), “Political” (moderate, ~10–15%), “Religious” (small, ~2–4%), plus very thin “Racial” and “Sexist” slices (each around ~1% or less). The outer ring further splits each middle-ring category into sentiment slices labeled “Negative,” “Neutral,” “Positive,” and “Mixed,” yielding many segments; visually, the largest outer segments include “Negative” under Abusive→Other and Abusive→Political, and “Positive” and “Neutral” under Not Abusive→Other, while many outer slices for Racial/Sexist/Religious are narrow slivers. Labels are placed directly on slices (no separate legend is shown), there are no numeric percentage annotations, and no slices appear exploded or offset; segment ordering follows the circular layout of the hierarchy rather than an obvious strict descending-size order.
